Article Title: 'Resignations are part of politics': DKS on two Congress MLAs quitting over Karnataka cabinet snub
Article Text:
I too was denied a ministerial berth, but didn't resign, said DK Shivakumar after 2 Congress MLAs quit.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Tuesday downplayed the resignation of two Congress MLAs who quit the legislative assembly after being left out of the state cabinet expansion, saying "it is a part of politics. "Shivakumar said, "Resignations are a part of politics. No one can stop those who want to resign. If they want the party and a political future, they should stay."Drawing from his own political journey, the chief minister said he too had been denied ministerial berths in the past but chose to remain with the party."If there is a party, everything else follows. When I was denied a ministerial berth during the tenures of Dharam Singh and Siddaramaiah, I could have resigned too. Didn't G Parameshwara and I remain patient?" he said.Shivakumar also said he had directed all ministers to immediately visit their respective districts to assess the drought relief situation.The remarks came a day after Congress MLAs Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned from the Karnataka Legislative Assembly, expressing disappointment over being excluded from the cabinet expansion.Patil submitted his resignation to Deputy Speaker Rudrappa Lamani at the Vidhana Soudha. Soon after, his supporters staged a protest in Bengaluru, alleging that he had been treated unfairly by the party.Gopalakrishna also resigned, adding to the pressure on the Congress leadership ahead of the swearing-in ceremony for the new ministers.Speaking to reporters, Patil claimed his name had been included in the list of ministers until the last moment but was dropped from the final announcement."I have been watching the developments within the party; ultimately today, during the expansion, our leadership failed to keep the promise made. So, without any other option, it was inevitable for me to resign. I have submitted the resignation," he said."It is not acceptable to my conscience. The situation in Vijayapura district is that loyalty and honesty are not valued in the Congress party . I have no other choice. I will speak to my supporters and well-wishers and decide on the future course of action," Patil said."I was promised a ministerial post even before the 2023 Assembly polls, but during the government formation, I was told it would happen after 2.5 years. They failed to keep the promise. I have no other choice. I'm not quitting the party, but they have created an atmosphere compelling me to resign," he added.The expansion comes around two months after DK Shivakumar assumed office as chief minister and is expected to be one of the biggest reshuffles in the state.
Article Summary: DK Shivakumar: "Resignations are a part of politics. No one can stop those who want to resign. If they want the party and a political future, they should stay" Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned.

Article Title: Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, who probed Babri Masjid demolition, dies at 87
Article Text:
Justice MS Liberhan (Picture from Haryana govt website)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, who headed the one-man commission that investigated the circumstances leading to the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya, died on Sunday at the age of 87.Punjab and Haryana high court bar association President Rohit Sud confirmed his death, saying Justice Liberhan passed away in Chandigarh. His last rites will be held on Monday.Justice Liberhan began practising law at the Punjab and Haryana high court in 1964. He was elected to the Punjab and Haryana Bar Council in August 1970 and remained a member until February 11, 1987. During this period, he also served as the Bar Council's secretary from January 1976 to June 1983.He was elevated as a judge of the Punjab and Haryana high court on February 11, 1987. In July 1997, he was appointed Chief Justice of the Madras high court before taking over as Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh high court in February 1998.On December 16, 1992, days after the demolition of the Babri Masjid, the Centre appointed Justice Liberhan to head the one-man Liberhan Commission to probe the events leading up to the incident. The commission went on to become one of the longest-running inquiries in India's history.
Article Summary: Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan died on Sunday at the age of 87. He headed the one-man commission that investigated the circumstances leading to the demolition of the Babri Masjid. The commission went on to become one of the longest-running inquiries in India's history.

Article Title: CRPF officer kills two colleagues, injures one before killing self in Assam
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A CRPF officer allegedly shot dead two of his colleagues and injured another before killing himself at a camp in Assam's Nagaon district on Tuesday, police told news agency PTI.The incident took place at the CRPF's 34 Battalion camp in Katimari, Nagaon, at around 7 am, when Assistant Sub-Inspector (GD) Ballani Premabaram, who was on duty at the main gate, allegedly opened fire on his colleagues, Nagaon Deputy Superintendent of Police (HQ) Paramita Sarkar told PTI.Premabaram later turned the weapon on himself and died at the spot, she said.Head Constable (GD) Vishnu Prasad Baghel and Sub-Inspector (GD) Ramnawal Singh Yadav were killed in the firing, while Assistant Sub-Inspector (Mane) Govind Sripul was injured and admitted to a private hospital for treatment.

Article Title: ‘Two sides of same coin’: Netaji’s grandnephew Chandra Bose quits TMC, takes swipe at BJP
Article Text:
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s grandnephew Chandra Kumar Bose resigned from the TMC on Monday, citing personal reasons, months after joining the party ahead of the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's grandnephew Chandra Kumar Bose on Monday resigned from the Trinamool Congress (TMC), saying he was "disillusioned" with mainstream political parties and saw "no difference" between the BJP and the Mamata Banerjee-led party.Bose, who joined the TMC barely four months ago ahead of the West Bengal assembly elections, said he would now mentor a proposed youth-led political platform based on the ideals of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose."I have been in the Forward Bloc, BJP and TMC. I am disillusioned with the mainstream political parties. They are all the same, just two sides of the same coin," Bose told PTI.He said the proposed platform would seek to offer an alternative to what he described as the politics of polarisation and confrontation."My politics is based on Netaji's ideology. We want to build a new political platform based on his principles of inclusive nationalism, secularism, social justice and development. I will mentor the youth who are coming together to form a party based on Netaji’s ideals," he added.There was no immediate reaction from the TMC to Bose's resignation.His exit marks another political shift for the former BJP state vice-president, who has repeatedly maintained that his politics is rooted in Netaji's ideology rather than party affiliation.Bose was earlier associated with the Forward Bloc, the party founded by Netaji. He joined the BJP in 2016 as the party expanded its political presence in West Bengal. He was subsequently appointed the party's state vice-president and contested the 2016 Assembly election and the 2019 Lok Sabha polls on a BJP ticket.His ties with the BJP later deteriorated. He was dropped as state vice-president during an organisational reshuffle in 2020 and increasingly voiced differences with the party leadership.Bose quit the BJP in 2023, claiming that the party had not lived up to its promise of advancing the inclusive nationalist ideals championed by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Sarat Chandra Bose.When he joined the TMC in April this year, Bose had criticised his former party over what he described as divisive politics and said the BJP's approach was contrary to the spirit of the Constitution."When I joined the Bharatiya Janata Party, I was made to understand that I could work to promote the ideology of Sarat Chandra Bose and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, which is inclusive and secular. India, as per the Constitution, is a sovereign, democratic, socialist, secular republic," he had said while joining the TMC.He had also described his decision to join the BJP as a "mistake" and said he hoped the TMC would provide a platform to uphold constitutional values and inclusive politics.Monday's resignation signals a similar disenchantment with the TMC, with Bose now seeking to build a political platform centred on Netaji's principles.Bose's political moves have attracted attention because of his family connection to Netaji and his sustained efforts to bring the freedom fighter's political philosophy into contemporary politics. Though he has not emerged as a mass electoral figure, he has consistently advocated what he describes as Netaji's vision of an inclusive India.Outside electoral politics, Bose has also campaigned for the preservation of Netaji's legacy. As spokesperson of the Open Platform for Netaji, he has led efforts seeking the declassification of files relating to the freedom fighter and greater public access to archival records concerning his life and disappearance.
Article Summary: Chandra Kumar Bose resigned from the Trinamool Congress (TMC) on Monday. He said he was "disillusioned" with mainstream political parties and saw "no difference" between the BJP and the Mamata Banerjee-led party. Bose joined the TMC barely four months ago ahead of the West Bengal assembly elections.

Article Title: WhatsApp puts multiple accounts under review, temporarily blocks access for users
Article Text:
A WhatsApp spokesperson acknowledged that errors can occur while enforcing the platform's safety measures.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Multiple WhatsApp users including several in India reported that their accounts had been placed "under review" for 24 hours, temporarily blocking access to the messaging platform's features without prior warning.The disruption surfaced around 8pm IST on Monday, with affected users sharing screenshots showing a message from the Meta-owned app stating that their accounts were being reviewed to verify compliance with WhatsApp's terms of service. The notification read that account activity and device information were being checked and that users would typically receive a decision within 24 hours.Responding a report by PTI, a WhatsApp spokesperson acknowledged that errors can occur while enforcing the platform's safety measures."We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting," the spokesperson said.The app also directed affected users to guidance on responsible use of WhatsApp and information relating to stolen phones and accounts.Several users took to social media to complain that their accounts had been disabled despite using the official version of the app.One user wrote: "My WhatsApp account has been disabled without any explanation. I have already submitted an appeal, but the review page only displays a generic message stating that it will 'typically be reviewed within 24 hours'. Help me urgently."Another user, identified as Saloni on X, posted: "My WhatsApp account was suddenly disabled without any warning. I only use the official app, and my work depends on WhatsApp. Please help. This was so unnecessary."The temporary account reviews come as WhatsApp remains under government scrutiny in India over its proposed username feature, which would allow users to communicate without sharing their phone numbers.The Centre recently received WhatsApp's response to a notice seeking clarification on the feature, which officials fear could increase phishing, impersonation, online fraud and so-called digital arrest scams. The government has directed the company not to roll out the feature in India until consultations are completed.WhatsApp has maintained that the feature is still under development and will be introduced gradually later this year. The company has said users will still need a phone number to create an account and that several safeguards, including protections against impersonation and limits on unsolicited contact, have been built into the feature.
Article Summary: Multiple WhatsApp users in India reported that their accounts had been placed "under review" for 24 hours. The disruption surfaced around 8pm IST on Monday, with affected users sharing screenshots. A WhatsApp spokesperson acknowledged that errors can occur while enforcing the platform's safety measures.

Article Title: Govt proposes mandatory Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication systems from Oct 2028 to cut road crashes
Article Text:
All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication system. (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From Oct 2028, all new two- and three-wheelers, cars, passenger and goods vehicles (including buses and trucks) would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication system, as per a draft notification of the road transport ministry. The V2V technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents.The recently published draft notification by road transport ministry proposes phased implementation of the V2V communication system and to start with all vehicles in categories L (two- and three-wheelers), M (passenger vehicles) and N (goods vehicles) manufactured from Oct 2027 would be required to comply with the newly-notified automotive standard, AIS-230, wherever they are equipped with V2V communication systems.The technology enables real-time exchange of speed, direction, position, and braking data between vehicles to prevent collisions at blind curves, intersections, or from drivers coming the wrong way without needing a cellular network. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.Unlike conventional vehicle-safety systems, which primarily depend on onboard sensors and driver reaction, V2V communication can provide information beyond the direct line of sight.“It is therefore expected to complement Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and support proactive accident prevention, connected mobility and future intelligent transport applications,” the ministry said.In this case, every vehicle fitted with the V2V communication system will continuously send out their locations, speed and direction as tiny radio signals. They will also relay information on sudden braking by a vehicle ahead, forward collision risks, unsafe lane changes, wrong-way driving and the approach of emergency vehicles.The receiving vehicle’s system compares this information with its own location, speed and direction to predict a possible collision and alerts the driver for action.At a later stage, govt will also roll out the Vehicle to Infrastructure (V2I) communication system. In this case, sensors are installed with infrastructure, such as signal and power poles, edges of bridges and flyovers, and barricaded areas to alert vehicles.
Article Summary: All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication system. The V2V technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.

JAMMU: At least 21 Bangladesh nationals, including four women and seven minors, were detained in J&K’s Ramban district last week. Officials were questioning them to learn who facilitated their movement to the Union Territory, official sources said Monday.The group was caught moving in two vehicles during a checking drive in Banihal on Aug 1, as no vehicle apart from those in Amarnath convoys is currently being allowed to move towards Kashmir in view of rain-triggered landslides and mudslides.Those detained are aged between two years and 38 years. “Upon verification, none of them could produce any valid identity or travel document establishing their lawful entry into or presence within Indian territory,” said an official source.“During preliminary questioning, the detained individuals disclosed that they had crossed the international border and entered India through Assam, from where they travelled to Jammu via train. They were moving towards Kashmir in search of employment,” the source added.Investigators were probing whether any local or interstate network was involved in assisting the movement of these illegal immigrants.

NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded at the New Delhi address of Independent MP Pappu Yadav Sunday after a man allegedly threw a slipper at him and another allegedly brandished a knife when he was holding a news conference.The accused, identified by sources as Sumit and Happy Sharma, are from Bulandshahr in UP. Members of Yadav’s team displayed before reporters the slipper and a knife which, they alleged, were used in the attack.Yadav alleged that it was a planned attempt on his life. “When the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. NEW DELHI: DMK Sunday mounted a furious pushback against Rahul Gandhi's describing any support to govt's widely speculated move to revive the bill to increase Lok Sabha's strength, coupled with delimitation of constituencies, as a betrayal of Tamil Nadu amid buzz in political circles that the regional party may come around to backing the measure.A day after Rahul, during his visit to Tamil Nadu, said any party supporting the constitution amendment bill in Parliament will be a 21st century Ettappan, a historical figure reviled for treachery, senior DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran came out with a blistering retort. Those who only talk about irregularities in the exam, rather than insisting on completely abolishing NEET are traitors. Those who condemn BJP's horse-trading but ignore TVK's disgusting horse-trading are merely continuing that betrayal."

Article Title: SC warns Punjab for ignoring 15-yr-old ruling on dues to Himachal Pradesh
Article Text:
Inter-state row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Punjab govt's stiff resistance to attorney general R Venkataramani's proposal for amicable implementation of a 15-year-old Supreme Court decree settling Bhakra Nangal and Beas power dues since 1966 in favour of Himachal Pradesh made SC observe, "The state has a habit of defying decrees and old habits die hard. "Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that he had extensive consultations with Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Union ministry of power after getting the records examined by CAG for independent determination of the historical capital cost liability."...a mutually workable settlement framework has been evolved. It envisages a cashless settlement, wherein the respective claims and liabilities are proposed to be adjusted through in-kind settlement of energy arrears and set-off of capital cost liability, thereby obviating the need for any direct financial transaction between the states," the AG said.Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Balbir Singh, appearing for Himachal and Haryana, respectively, said they were agreeable with the AG's settlement proposal for implementation of the decree, which was passed by the SC in 2011 on an original suit filed by Himachal 30 years ago seeking settlement of assets on division of Punjab in 1966.For Punjab, senior advocate Nidhesh Gupta said the state had key concerns over workability of the AG's proposal and said the state would stand to lose substantially.Given the fact that it is a 15-year-old decree passed on a 30-year-old original suit seeking resolution of a 60-year-old inter-state dispute, the bench said, "Your state has a habit of defying decrees...""There is a decree in Himachal's favour. When we order implement, it will be with interest from 2011. We will not allow them to be deprived of the fruits of the decree. If you settle, it is well and good. Otherwise, be ready for consequences." It posted the matter for hearing on Aug 12.In its July 30 order, the bench said, "While the states of Himachal and Haryana have graciously agreed in principle to the proposal, the state of Punjab has raised objections thereto. In the interest of justice, two weeks time is granted to Punjab to reconsider and clarify its stand."The AG's proposal had said, "Punjab and Haryana will provide 13,066 MU of energy arrears to HP at 871 MU per annum over 15 lean seasons (Oct-March), in the inter-se ratio of 58:42 (Bhakra Nangal project) and 60:40 (Beas projects). HP to pay BBMB-determined charges for the year in which each tranche is received."HP's liability (7.19% of composite Punjab) towards the capital cost of Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects - being the unreimbursed share of loan servicing by Punjab and Haryana since 1966-67 - be assessed at Rs 420.7 crore (Punjab: Rs 249.2 crore; Haryana: Rs 171.5 crore). The capital cost liability could be considered to set off against part of HP's energy arrear receivables.At the rate of Rs 3.85 per unit, the units to be offset is approximately 1093 MUs. "SC on Sept 27, 2011 (Justices R V Raveendran and A K Patnaik) had decreed the suit in favour of HP by ruling, "The state is entitled to 7.19% of the power of the composite state of Punjab from the Bhakra Nangal project with effect from Nov 1, 1966, and from Beas project with effect from the dates of production in Unit I and Unit II."
Article Summary: Punjab govt's stiff resistance to amicable implementation of 15-year-old Supreme Court decree. Decree settled Bhakra Nangal and Beas power dues since 1966 in favour of Himachal Pradesh. "The state has a habit of defying decrees and old habits die hard," says SC.

Article Title: Withdraw cases, allow youngsters to continue studies: SC to states
Article Text:
The Supreme Court permitted governments to withdraw cases against student protesters.

Want to lay down norms on use of graded force, says SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for the dropping of cases against student protesters, Supreme Court on Monday permitted Delhi and state govts to withdraw or close FIRs lodged during NEET paper leak protests in different parts of India and said these youngsters must be allowed to pursue their studies without the fear of getting prosecuted.The bench clarified its July 28 order in which it had stayed coercive action against student protesters but permitted police to proceed with the investigations. This had created an apprehension in the minds of students about the future consequences of the cases remaining live.The go-ahead came after solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that “govt is serious about honouring the commitment (given to CJP) on withdrawal of cases against student protesters. We are discussing the modalities of dropping cases”.However, Mehta said that FIRs registered during student protests against 2,738 people who had criminal antecedents – having been accused of rape, murder and child sexual abuse under Pocso Act — and had infiltrated the protests to indulge in violence and vandalism will not be dropped. The bench said the rider would apply to those accused of heinous and grave offences and not petty offences or political cases.Mehta said, “Those who were leading the protests are again in touch with govt to work out the modalities for dropping cases against genuine student protesters as withdrawal of cases may not be possible under the law.” The top court posted the matter for further hearing on Aug 18.CJI Kant was firm that student protesters must be freed from the fear of future prosecution. He said, “Parameters for students are altogether different. Their cases should be considered in a different manner so that they remain in the mainstream and their education is not disturbed.“The parents are spending their hard-earned money on their children’s education. We must not keep aside the expectations of the parents of these youngsters. If the children are unnecessarily dragged into such (police and court) processes, it is not going to serve any purpose,” the CJI said.The solicitor general agreed and said modalities for the withdrawal/dropping of cases against student protesters will be worked out soon. He added, “There will be some people who would like to keep the pot boiling — we must be very careful even while taking legal steps.”Justice Bagchi said that when the parties agree to it, the court can engender and enable the process so that the FIRs do not remain hanging over students’ heads.Senior advocate Vrinda Grover said both CJP leaders and other students are in talks with the SG and govt to chart out an agreed modality for the dropping of cases. She cited a Patna FIR registered against 142 people and 5,000 unknown persons, and said this appeared to be ‘catch all’ tactics to pick up anyone randomly in the future. A comprehensive mechanism needs to be evolved, she said.Justice Bagchi said, “There are many options. The prosecution can file a closure report, the public prosecutor can advise withdrawal of cases or we can quash the FIRs.”The CJI-led bench said that while the violence and police excesses would be investigated by an SIT, “we want to lay down comprehensive guidelines for the future on use of graded force, whether it should include pellet guns or not, after getting recommendations from the high-powered committee we intend to constitute”.Senior advocate Shyam Divan said the committee/commission should be headed by a retired CJI. The bench said getting a former CJI to head the committee is difficult, and it will be chaired by a former SC judge. It asked Delhi Police, Centre and states to file their responses to the petition and give their suggestions on the terms of reference of the committee.Senior advocate N Hariharan questioned how Delhi Police could identify 2,738 criminals among the protesters and said they must have used face recognition devices on all protesters and profiled them, which is a serious violation of privacy of the individuals guaranteed under Article 21.
Article Summary: Supreme Court permitted Delhi and state govts to withdraw or close FIRs lodged during NEET paper leak protests in different parts of India. The bench clarified its July 28 order in which it had stayed coercive action against student protesters but permitted police to proceed with investigations.

NEW DELHI: The population enumeration phase of Census 2027 — which will capture caste for the first time since 1931, and most likely also record the date and birthplace of parents, along with the respondent’s passport number (where available) and Aadhaar number (voluntary) — will start in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand on August 17.A home ministry notification on Monday said the population enumeration exercise in snow-bound areas of the four northern states/UTs will run from Sept 1 to 30, preceded by a self-enumeration window of August 17-30. This means that the questionnaire for Phase 2 of Census will also be notified soon.According to sources, caste will be recorded ‘as declared by the respondent’. There will be a drop-down menu for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, while the ‘caste’ field will only cater to those in non-SC, non-ST category. The drop-down menu will only show the SC/ST list of the state where the respondent is being enumeratedThe spelling of the declared ‘caste’ will be recorded as cited by the respondent. No document or caste certificate is required to be shown to verify one’s SC, ST or ‘caste’ status. An officer said while the self-declaration template followed for the socio-economic caste census (SECC) in 2011 had thrown up over 45,000 castes, making the data unusable, modern digital tools and AI can now surmount compilation and segregation challenges.Census Phase 2, in a first, , will collect the date and place of birth of parents, the key factors that determine citizenship/nationality.The national population register (NPR) exercise — conducted alongside Census 2011, intended to be repeated with Census 2021 before it was postponed, but now delinked from Census 2027 — had in 2010 collected details of nationality as declared by the respondent, with the rider that it would not confer any right of citizenship.Sources said the respondents will not be asked for proof of birth details of parents and these would be recorded “to the best knowledge of the respondent”. In fact, where the respondents do not know the exact date of birth of parents but only the year, a default date like January 1 of that year will be accepted.The Phase 2 questionnaire will also log passport details where available. Aadhaar number will be collected on a voluntary basis.“The purpose of collecting the birth data of parents is to know the total number of people who meet citizenship criteria based on their declaration, even though unverified. It will have no impact on the individual as the Census Act does not allow individual data to be used for “legal evidence, govt benefits or public disclosure,” said an officer.Self-enumeration option for Phase 2, unlike Phase 1, may allow users to submit partially-filed enumeration forms, provided a minimum number of questions are answered. “There is a realisation that even if some data fields are self-enumerated, the task of the enumerator becomes easier and less time-consuming,” said an officer.As per convention, the population enumeration exercise — which records individual data like marital status, religion, SC/ST status, occupation, migration and fertility, besides arriving at the country’s headcount — is conducted nationwide in February of the census reference year. However, it is advanced in pockets that face extreme cold and inclement weather during this window.
Article Summary: The population enumeration phase of Census 2027 will start in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand on August 17. The Census is also likely to collect passport numbers (where available) and Aadhaar numbers voluntarily.

Article Title: SC expands ambit of Sec 498A to cover cruelty in live-ins too
Article Text:
SC said that cruelty does not distinguish between married and unmarried women

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Saying that "live-in relationships" are a reality particularly in urban areas and the law must adapt itself to serve those who choose this form of relationship and protect them from harassing partners, the Supreme Court Monday brought them under the ambit of Section 498A of the IPC or Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) where a husband or in-law shall be punished with imprisonment for a term up to three years for subjecting a woman to cruelty.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and N K Singh rejected the plea that 498A is confined only to a husband married to a woman in the traditional sense. "Since the provision was aimed at solving a societal issue, it is this larger objective of securing equality for women, stepping away from the superiority of males that is an inheritance from bygone days, that has to inform the understanding in interpretation and implementation of the Section," SC said.It, however, clarified that only those "live-in relationships" which are in the nature of marriage will come within the ambit of Section 498A of IPC or Sec 85 of BNS. "Cruelty does not check at the door whether the house it's entering is that of a married woman or not. Once it enters, its propensity to destroy is aggravated," it said.SC, however, took note of the growing instances of alleged misuse of Section 498A. Describing as worrisome the trend of the section being misused and employed as a means of settling scores and ventilating grievances, SC said its verdict would be applicable to only those 'relationships in the nature of marriage' and the initial burden of proof would be on the female live-in partner seeking protection of the law."When the objective of the Section 498A was to provide coverage to those cases where harassment by husband or in-laws through wilful conduct causing mental or physical injury or driving the woman to suicide, then to say that such harassment can only be caused when they are married and not before that, in our considered view, would be a case of over simplification. Whether or not the woman in question is married or not, in the present day, does not have a proximate link to the objective of the section, which is to prevent cruelty in such a household setting," Justice Karol, who penned the verdict, said.The court said the law must respond to changing times, and bringing live-in relations within the ambit of Section 498A is needed. "Marriage was considered to be sacrosanct, which undoubtedly is a changing phenomenon. Living together, prior to marriage, is not unheard of or unacceptable anymore. In the same way, that same-sex relations, once criminalised and deemed to be a mental illness, have now been decriminalised and recognised as naturally occurring.This is the evolution of societal standards," SC said."Not a single person goes into a relationship knowing or anticipating that cruelty may be meted out to them. When a couple sets out on their journey, it is always, one presumes, with the best of intentions and to bring joyfulness of all forms. With the passage of time, however, some relationships may go down this troublesome path. The law must provide for the same. This distinction between "married" and "live-in relationship in the nature of marriage", in as much as it relates to the protection envisaged by Section 498A, has no rational nexus with the object of preventing domestic violence and is as such offensive to Article 14 of the Constitution," the bench said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court said that cruelty does not distinguish between married and unmarried women. Justices Sanjay Karol and N K Singh rejected the plea that 498A is confined only to a husband married to a woman in the traditional sense. SC said its verdict would be applicable to only those'relationships in the nature of marriage' and the initial burden of proof would be on the female live-in partner seeking protection.

Article Title: UPS has attracted just 4% of NPS subscribers: Government

NEW DELHI: For all the noise demanding an assurance on pension, Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for central govt employees has received low traction.Data shared with Parliament Monday estimated the number of govt employees, including those who joined recently, at 1,18,195 on July 19 — which is 4.3% of the 27.6 lakh central govt number subscribers of National Pension Trust at the end of June.For long govt employees, at the Centre as well as in states, were demanding an assurance that the pension payout be at least 50% of their last salary — something that is the norm under the old pension scheme, which was discontinued in 2004 when NPS, which has contributions from the employee, kicked in.Several opposition-governed states stopped contributing to NPS and wanted to opt out, prompting the Centre to put in place UPS from April 2025. Article Title: South drives CM wealth surge as four leaders hold 91% of assets
Article Text:
Analysis of ADR report

South pulls the wealth map

Analysing the assets held by CMs

Same party, different worlds

Younger leaders, uneven party trend

India now has younger CMs

Degrees stay broadly stable

Cases rise, but cluster in five names

Criminal cases against CMs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Politics often comes wrapped in familiar assumptions. With the BJP, the ruling party at the Centre, now also in power in a majority of states, either alone or in alliance, one might expect a degree of sameness in the profiles of India’s chief ministers. Yet the Association for Democratic Reforms reports show a more varied picture. The country’s CMs come from different social strata, age groups, educational backgrounds and economic profiles, even within their own parties. There is no single formula for political ascent.That is what makes the comparison between ADR’s 2025 and 2026 reports more revealing than either report viewed alone. The 2025 study examined 30 chief ministers, since Manipur was then under President’s Rule. The 2026 report covers 31, after the return of a chief minister in the state. More importantly, the occupants of the chief minister’s office changed in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar and West Bengal.The combined assets declared by India’s chief ministers rose from Rs 1,632 crore in the 2025 report to Rs 3,660 crore in 2026. Average assets more than doubled from Rs 54.42 crore to Rs 118.07 crore. The number of billionaire chief ministers rose from two to four.In 2025, N Chandrababu Naidu, with assets of Rs 931.84 crore, and Pema Khandu , with Rs 332.57 crore, were the only billionaire chief ministers. Siddaramaiah was a distant third with Rs 51.94 crore. A year later, Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar is the clear number one with Rs 1,413.8 crore, while cine star and Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay declared assets of Rs 648.86 crore. Together, these four account for approximately Rs 3,327 crore, or 90.9% of the assets declared by all 31 chief ministers. The remaining 27 account for only around Rs 333 crore between them.A geographical cut makes the imbalance sharper. Using a broad four-zone grouping, not an ADR classification, the South has only six of the 31 CMs but accounts for roughly Rs 3,059 crore, or about 83.6% of all declared CM assets in 2026. That is because three of the four billionaire CMs, Shivakumar, Naidu and Vijay, are from southern states. So the South, in a way, lives up to the larger-than-life CM personalities. Naidu is a veteran politician who has survived many ebbs to rise again and regain his lost glory. D K Shivakumar finally got rewarded after a power tussle with Siddaramaiah, and Vijay was the new kid on the block who broke through the DMK-AIADMK binary, while also ticking the box of another cine star to become CM of Tamil Nadu. So the profiles of these billionaire CMs could not be more different.East and the Northeast together have the largest number of CMs in this grouping, 12, but account for about Rs 495 crore, helped substantially by Khandu’s declaration. North and Central India together have 10 CMs but only around Rs 75 crore in declared assets, while the West has three CMs and around Rs 31 crore.The party-wise picture is just as uneven. The BJP has 17 chief ministers in the 2026 list, but they are far from a single economic bloc. Its richest CM is Pema Khandu, with Rs 332.57 crore in declared assets. Its poorest is West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, with about Rs 85.88 lakh. That is a nearly 387-fold gap within the same party.The Congress spread is smaller in headcount but sharper in scale. Of its four CMs, Shivakumar alone accounts for Rs 1,413.8 crore. At the other end is Kerala CM V D Satheesan, with Rs 6.66 crore. Revanth Reddy , at Rs 30.05 crore, and Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhvinder Singh, at Rs 7.82 crore, sit far below Shivakumar’s level. In effect, Congress’s CM asset profile is overwhelmingly shaped by one leader.This is why the average can mislead. A calculation based on individual entries puts the 2026 median at only around Rs 8.23 crore, barely higher than the 2025 median of about Rs 8.02 crore.Total declared liabilities rose from roughly Rs 242 crore in 2025 to nearly Rs 505 crore in 2026, though the number of CMs declaring liabilities of Rs 1 crore or more remained unchanged at 11. Khandu led the 2025 liability table with Rs 180.28 crore. In 2026, Shivakumar moved to the top with Rs 265.07 crore, followed by Khandu and Himanta Biswa Sarma.The leadership profile also became younger. In 2025, 12 of the 30 chief ministers were in the 51-60 group. By 2026, that number had risen to 17. The number aged 61 or above fell from 10 to six. The 41-50 category remained unchanged at eight.The average reported age declined from 58.8 to 56.7, though the median remained 56. The shift reflects the exit of several older CMs, including Siddaramaiah, Pinarayi Vijayan, Nitish Kumar , M K Stalin and Mamata Banerjee. The ages are those recorded when election affidavits were filed, not necessarily current ages. So the actual decline is much sharper because the 2025 calculation accounted for many outgoing CMs’ 2021 affidavits.Here again, parties differ internally. Congress’s four CMs are tightly bunched. Revanth Reddy is 56, Sukhvinder Singh 58, Shivakumar 60 and Satheesan 61. The BJP’s spread is wider. It has Pema Khandu at 44 and Manik Saha at 70, with several CMs clustered in their 50s. In other words, the Congress CM cohort is smaller and more middle-aged, while the BJP’s larger pool stretches from younger leadership to older veterans.There was a reversal on gender. The 2025 report listed two women among 30 chief ministers. The 2026 report lists only one among 31. Mamata Banerjee’s exit from the CM roster left Delhi’s Rekha Gupta as the sole woman in the group.Many of the politicians are products of student politics. They may not have worked professionally, but they still believed in the inherent importance of formal education. In 2025, 25 of the 30 CMs were graduates, professional graduates, postgraduates or doctorate holders. In 2026, the number remained 25, despite the larger group. The proportion with graduate-level qualification or higher slipped slightly, from about 83% to 81%.Within parties, the BJP shows the widest educational spread. Its CM list includes doctorate holders such as Mohan Yadav, Himanta Biswa Sarma and Samrat Choudhary, but also leaders listed as Class 10 pass, diploma holders, graduates, professional graduates and postgraduates. Congress’s four CMs are more compact educationally: Shivakumar and Sukhvinder Singh are postgraduates, Revanth Reddy is a graduate and Satheesan is a graduate professional.The criminal-record figures worsened modestly. In 2025, 12 of 30 chief ministers, or 40%, had declared criminal cases; 10 had cases classified by ADR as serious. By 2026, 14 of 31, or 45%, had declared criminal cases; 11 had serious cases.The combined number of declared cases rose from 187 to 195. The burden remained concentrated. Revanth Reddy continued to head the list with 89 cases, followed by Suvendu Adhikari with 29, Shivakumar and Naidu with 19 each, and Kerala’s V D Satheesan with 18. Five chief ministers accounted for 174 of the 195 cases, or 89.2%.Three of Congress’s four CMs are among the top five by declared cases: Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar and Satheesan. Among BJP CMs, Adhikari carries the highest declared case load, while several BJP chief ministers have no declared criminal cases. Geography shows a similar concentration, though for different reasons. The six southern CMs together account for 147 declared cases, driven mainly by Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar, Naidu and Satheesan. East and the Northeast account for 38 cases, led by Adhikari. North and Central India account for six, while the West accounts for four. It is perhaps not a coincidence that many of the CMs with high case loads were opposition leaders for a significant time.Thus, criminal cases need to be treated with caution. A low case count may not strictly be a virtue; it may just be a case of friendly police administration.Disclosures aren’t the only way to understand the nature of a politician. But they are an important starting point, particularly when compared over the years, to understand how the seat of power remains the same, but the nature of those who occupy it changes, perhaps as an inevitable reflection of the realities of the times.
Article Summary: The number of billionaire chief ministers rose from two to four. Average assets more than doubled from Rs 54.42 crore to Rs 118.07 crore. Three of the four billionaire CMs, Shivakumar, Naidu and Vijay, are from southern states.

Article Title: After success of students protest, Kisan Morcha plans to hit streets
Article Text:
Samyukt Kisan Morcha announced Monday that it would restart protests at 100 locations across India, including Delhi, from Nov 26.

NEW DELHI: Emboldened by the success of student protests at Jantar Mantar, Samyukt Kisan Morcha - the umbrella organisation of farmer groups involved in the anti-farm laws agitation five years ago - announced Monday that it would restart protests at 100 locations across India, including Delhi, from Nov 26.The protesters will demand a law guaranteeing MSP; repeal of all FTAs, including the India-US FTA currently under negotiation; a comprehensive loan waiver to address rural indebtedness; scrapping of four labour codes; minimum wage of Rs 31,000 for workers and restoration of the old rural job guarantee scheme; withdrawal of Electricity Privatisation Bill 2025, Seed Bill 2025 and NFSA Amendment Bill; and no forceful land acquisition."The protests will not be called off till all seven demands are accepted," said P Krishnaprasad of AIKS.
Article Summary: Samyukt Kisan Morcha announced Monday that it would restart protests at 100 locations across India, including Delhi, from Nov 26. The protesters will demand a law guaranteeing MSP; repeal of all FTAs, including the India-US FTA currently under negotiation.

Article Title: J&K: Days after Kulgam terror attack, man with grenade held in Pulwama
Article Text:
Kulgam: Security personnel keep a vigil during an inspection of vehicles to maintain public safety following the recent terror attack in Anantnag, at Qaimoh, Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: A suspect was arrested Monday in J&K’s Pulwama with a hand grenade, three “anti-national” posters and a mobile phone during a security overdrive spurred by last week’s killings of two migrant labourers in a terror attack in neighbouring Kulgam.Police identified the man as Tousef Ahmad Dar, a local, and booked him under several laws, including the stringent Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).Authorities claimed Dar was spotted walking towards a checkpoint set up jointly by J&K police, Army and CRPF and began to flee after noticing the security forces. Dar was chased down by troopers and caught some distance away, the police said.“The police remain committed to maintaining peace and security and will continue to take firm action against individuals involved in anti-national and unlawful activities,” the police said in a statement.The checkpoint where Dar was spotted is one of many across Kashmir that have come up after the killings of the two migrant workers on July 31.Earlier, on July 23, a terrorist shot dead a J&K head constable, Ashiq Hussain Qureshi, in south Kashmir’s Anantnag. It was the first attack in Kashmir since the Pahalgam massacre that left 26 people, most of them tourists, dead on April 22 last year. The police said Lashkar-e-Toiba offshoot The Resistance Front (TRF) was involved in both the Kulgam and Anantnag attacks.On Monday, Kashmir IG VK Birdi reviewed security and ordered robust counter-insurgency measures. “He (Virdi) stressed seamless coordination among all agencies. The IGP also reviewed security for highways, rail tracks and stations across the Valley. He directed officers to place “dynamic nakas” and ensure enhanced foot patrolling, particularly at night, at vulnerable locations and inter-district boundaries,” a police spokesman said.
Article Summary: Tousef Ahmad Dar, a local, was arrested in J&K’s Pulwama with a hand grenade, three ‘anti-national’ posters and a mobile phone. Dar was chased down by troopers and caught some distance away, police said. Kashmir IG VK Birdi reviewed security and ordered robust counter-insurgency measures.

Article Title: A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Prashant Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for both BJP and RJD
Article Text:
Prashant Kishor celebrates after winning the Bankipur Assembly bypoll (Image credit: PTI)

BJP has held Bankipur assembly seat from 1995 (Till 2005, the seat was known as Patna West)

BJP chief Nitin Nabin won from the Bankipur assembly seat four times in a row

Nitin Nabin won from Bankipur for first time in 2010 with a margin of 56%

From 1995 to 2010, the seat (known as Patna West) was represented by Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha (Nitin Nabin’s father)

Father-son duo has won the seat 8 consecutive times

‘Bankipur’s message to BJP central leadership’

Prashant Kishor hits out at Bihar CM

Kishor's development pitch or disappointment against BJP?

‘Verdict by Bihar's youth against BJP’

Shock verdict for BJP

Lalu's RJD pushed to fringes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Time to pause, review

Poll Vote & Share your view Is it time for RJD to reevaluate its strategies after the bypoll results? Yes, they need a clear plan No, they should stick to current strategies 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor has finally found a seat for his “school bag” in Bihar. The election strategist-turned-politician, whose party contests on a school bag symbol, has flipped the Bankipur assembly seat, an unassailable bastion of the BJP for the last 30 years. Before today’s shock defeat, the BJP had registered 8 consecutive victories in Bankipur since 1995, when it won the seat for the first time.By-election in Bankipur was necessitated after Nitin Nabin resigned as BJP MLA from the seat in April after his election to Rajya Sabha. This followed Nitin Nabin’s elevation as BJP national president in January this year.To gauge the enormity of Prashant Kishor’s victory, look at these facts:For PK, as Prashant Kishor is popularly known, contesting the Bankipur byelection was a huge political gamble. PK, who made a high-pitched entry into Bihar politics with a padyatra spanning months ahead of the 2025 assembly elections, cut a sorry figure when his Jan Suraj Party failed to win even one seat less than a year ago. Such dismal was his first electoral show that JSP lost deposit in 236 of the 238 seats it contested. Prashant Kishor did not contest the election himself and instead led a high-voltage campaign for his party across the state.Little wonder his decision to contest the Bankipur bypoll was fraught with the danger of becoming a make-or-break political move. But the gamble has paid off and Prashant Kishor with his debut win has propelled into the centrestage of Bihar politics.Prashant Kishor polled over 64,151 votes and won the key electoral battle by a margin of 19,324 votes over BJP’s Neeraj Kumar. Prashant Kishor’s resounding success, nine months after his party’s humiliating defeat, marks a remarkable turnaround.And making the most of his victory, Prashant Kishor immediately trained his guns at Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary."This is the victory of the people of Bankipur. As we stated during the election campaign, this was not just an election to choose an MLA. It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the chief minister of Bihar. They do not want a person with a criminal background or questionable conduct, character, or reputation to lead Bihar. They want a good chief minister who can improve education, create employment opportunities for the youth, and ensure that the children of Bihar do not have to migrate elsewhere for work," Kishor told reporters as his supporters celebrated his maiden electoral victory.Prashant Kishor’s use of his victory to target Samrat Choudhary did not come as a surprise. Ksihor been unrelenting in his attacks against the BJP leader ever since the election strategist became a full-time politician. He has targeted Samrat Choudhary over the chief minister’s educational qualification and his alleged criminal past.The Jan Suraaj chief also called upon the BJP's central leadership to focus on governance ahead of the next Lok Sabha elections, stating, "Before the Lok Sabha elections, Prime Minister Modi, the BJP, and Amit Shah should focus on improving Bihar, creating jobs for its youth, and stopping migration. That is our only objective. We do not want to become MLAs merely to award contracts. Our sole objective is the development of Bihar. "These are the very themes on which Prashant Kishor fought the 2025 assembly elections and lost. Clearly, while he keeps focus on these issues, his victory in bankipur may less be about endorsement of his development focus and more about people’s disappointment with the BJP. The result is also perhaps a fallout of the students’ agitation against NEET-UG paper leak, which saw huge protests in Bihar. In Siwan, a police constable was suspended after a video purportedly showing him using an AK-47 rifle during a student protest on July 25 went viral on social media.Leader of opposition in Bihar assembly, Tejashwi Yadav , slammed Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for the incident. He posted a video of the purported incident on X and, along with it, said, "During the protest in Siwan, police resorted to direct firing with an AK-47 on students. When a criminal becomes chief minister, then police fire bullets at innocent students.”CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya in his message to Prashant Kishor described his victory as a significant verdict by Bihar's youth against the BJP-led state government.In a post on X, Bhattacharya termed Kishor's victory a "well-earned debut victory" and said the bypoll result reflected public anger against the ruling dispensation."Congratulations to Prashant Kishor on his well-earned debut victory in Bankipur bypoll. Kudos to the youth of Bihar for delivering such a telling blow to the supremely arrogant, incompetent and tyrannical BJP government of Bihar," he said.The BJP was quick to accept the verdict of the people. State BJP president Sanjay Saraogi said in a statement, "We bow before the will of the people. We shall draw lessons from the debacle, unlike our opponents who tend to blame every electoral loss of theirs on EVMs and the Election Commission".But for the BJP, this defeat comes as an embarrassment for both its national president Nitin Nabin and the party’s first chief minister in the state Samrat Choudhary. Bankipur seat was literally a personal fiefdom of Nitin Nabin’s family which represented the constituency for 30 long years. A defeat in the backyard will surely embarrass the BJP chief.For Samrat Choudhary, this was the first electoral test of his government which was formed after the BJP took over the reins of the state from JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar. It was Nitish Kumar who had led the NDA to an emphatic triumph in the 2025 assembly elections. And the BJP would have hoped that Samrat Choudhary would have given it a winning start. But that was not to be.The Bankipur bypoll result also has a worrying message for the main opposition party RJD. Tejashwi Yadav’s party seems to have learnt no lessons from the 2025 electoral drubbing. The party which has been reduced to 25 seats in the assembly did little to show intent on the ground.Its candidate Rekha Kumari polled just 14,273 votes. This was over 32,000 votes less than the figure of 46,363, which she had polled in the 2025 assembly elections as the runnerup in the seat. Ironically, for the greater part of the campaign, RJD’s star campaigner Tejashwi Yadav was missing in action.It may not be prudent to overexaggerate the outcome of one bypoll. The result of one seat, even though high-profile, may not be indicative of any larger trend. But for the BJP and the RJD to brush aside the defeat as a one-off setback would be doing harm to their cause. The BJP should remember that it rules Bihar but is still dependent on its allies for survival. The RJD, meanwhile, remains the main opposition party but seems to have lost the plot to factionalism and family feuds after its dismal 2025 show. Both need to pause and review what went wrong in Bankipur. MLA Prashant Kishor, on the other hand, will perhaps be now preparing for another bout with his political bete noir Samrat Choudhary - this time on the floor of Bihar assembly.
Article Summary: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor has finally found a seat for his “school bag” in Bihar. Article Title: India crosses 20k organ transplants/yr for 1st time

Deceased donor transplants still far short of demand

NEW DELHI: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, crossing the 20,000-mark for the first time and registered a 6.5% increase over the previous year, according to National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation’s (NOTTO) annual report. The figure marks a fourfold rise from 4,990 transplants in 2013.Delhi-NCR recorded the highest number of transplants in 2025 with 4,564 procedures, followed by Tamil Nadu (2,796), Maharashtra (2,136), Telangana (1,523) and Kerala (1,489). Tamil Nadu topped the country in deceased organ donors with 266, followed by Maharashtra (205), Telangana (198), Karnataka (154) and Kerala (152).India has emerged as the world’s third-largest country in total organ transplants, after the US and China.India continues to rank first globally in living donor organ transplants, according to Global Observatory on Donation and Transplantation report released in 2026.The 20,000-mark milestone coincided with the 16th Indian Organ Donation Day, when health ministry announced that more than five lakh Aadhaar-verified organ donation pledges have been recorded since the national digital pledge portal was launched in 2023.Despite the gains, deceased organ donation remains India’s biggest challenge. Deceased donor transplants rose from 837 in 2013 to 3,526 in 2025, but continue to fall far short of demand. “A substantial gap still exists between demand for organs and their availability. Addressing this gap remains a national priority,” MoS for health Anupriya Patel said.To strengthen the programme, govt launched ‘Jug Jug Jiyo Abhiyaan’, a year-long awareness campaign, besides rolling out e-Pratyaropan, a digital platform for donor registration, waitlist management and organ allocation, NOTTO mobile app, and new Brain Stem Death Certification and Swap Transplantation guidelines.Govt has also expanded transplant services, with 10 new AIIMS now performing kidney transplants, while AIIMS Bhopal has started heart transplantation and AIIMS Jodhpur, Bhubaneswar, Patna, Rishikesh have launched liver transplant programmes.The report highlights reforms under ‘One Nation, One Policy’ initiative, including removal of domicile requirements, the upper age limit and registration fees for patients seeking deceased donor organs. With nearly 1.73 lakh road traffic fatalities every year, the report says India has significant potential to increase deceased organ donation.
Article Summary: India has emerged as the world’s third-largest country in total organ transplants, after the US and China. Tamil Nadu topped the country in deceased organ donors with 266, followed by Maharashtra (205), Telangana (198), Karnataka (154) and Kerala (152)

Article Title: Meta CEO Zuckerberg must apologise: Parliamentary Panel
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Rejecting Meta's apology for taking down a PM Narendra Modi's video, a parliamentary committee Monday sought a personal apology from its founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg and warned of seeking removal of its safe harbour protection if he failed to comply, its chairperson Nishikant Dubey said.Dubey said removal of the PM's video was either a serious failure of the system or there "is a deliberate attempt to tarnish the image of the PM" on part of Meta."If this is how they deal with the official post of the PM, what can the common people of India expect? This failure cannot be dismissed merely as a technical error. It is a serious matter and an apology must come from Zuckerberg's side. And if he does not apologise, safe harbour protection should be taken back from them," Dubey said.Senior representatives of a host of social media platforms, including X, Google, YouTube, besides Meta, appeared before the Dubey-led committee on communications and IT, besides home secretary Govind Mohan and IT secretary S Krishnan.Parliamentarians questioned digital platforms over their choice of algorithms and presence of unlawful content, including child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deep fake investment scams, and targeting of women, with Meta being particularly at the receiving end of their ire.While some opposition MPs emphasised that social media must retain space of dissent and 'anti-govt' content should not be considered 'anti-national', the committee was unanimous in asking for stricter and timely measures against the content that are in violation of their own stated policies, especially involving CSAM, cyber frauds, and harassment of women."We are unanimous and non-partisan on all issues," Dubey said, adding that even MHA's communications is ignored by these platforms.The BJP MP referred to the high online viewership grabbed by CJP during its recent protest, saying it, at 27 million, was more than the combined viewership of parties like BJP, Congress, AAP and SP. He blamed the platforms' choice of algorithm favouring new entrants for this.Some MPs demanded that Meta must fix accountability for removing Modi's video, which was restored later by the social media behemoth, which owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.Social media platforms can amplify or suppress any content's reach, remove it or attach community notes that carry abuses, and then the question is whether they are mere intermediaries as they claim or publishers, Dubey said."It is disturbing that in 2025 alone approximately 28.15 lakh cybercrime complaints were reported nationally, with estimated losses of nearly Rs 22,495 crore," he added.
Article Summary: Parliamentarians questioned digital platforms over their choice of algorithms and presence of unlawful content. MPs demanded that Meta must fix accountability for removing Modi's video, which was restored later by the social media behemoth. Senior representatives of a host of social media platforms, including X, Google, YouTube, besides Meta, appeared before the committee on communications and IT.

Article Title: ARAI's study on E20 fuel impact may be made public

NEW DELHI: Amid growing demand to make the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) study report on E20 fuel's impact on E10-compatible vehicles public, govt agencies are looking at the possibility to release it to help remove misconceptions among vehicle users .TOI has learnt that since specific two-wheelers and cars were used for the study, details of models may not be disclosed considering commercial interest of vehicle manufacturers. "Govt has referred to the study and its findings to respond to questions in Parliament. Hence, there is a view that it should be made public so that people see that E20 fuel doesn't impact engines," said an official.In June 2021, petroleum ministry had directed ARAI and IOCL, in association with SIAM, to carry out the study. The study had concluded that in case of E10-compliant two-wheelers, fuel consumption increased in the range of 1-6% and mass emission met the regulatory requirement. In the case of BS-IV cars, fuel consumption increased by 2-4%, and 2-3% in case of BS-VI-compliant cars.

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has suspended the licence of a packaged drinking water manufacturer in Tripura and prohibited the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of a dietary food supplement made by a Punjab-based company after inspections found serious food safety and regulatory violations.The licence of M/S Matri Drinking Water, Gomati, Tripura, was suspended with immediate effect following a complaint about foreign material in packaged drinking water. Inspectors found finished products stored outside the facility and on the floor alongside non-food materials, unhygienic processing and filling areas, rusted RO water storage tanks and chemical dosing containers, inadequate pest control and sanitation, and the absence of mandatory testing, maintenance and training records. A qualified technical supervisor was also not available during the inspection.In a separate action, FSSAI prohibited the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of Venolex Forte, marketed by M/S Noble Healthcare, Mohali, saying the dietary food supplement contained ingredients not permitted under the Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food and Novel Food) Regulations, 2022.The regulator said the product contained pharmacologically active ingredients, including calcium dobesilate, diosmin and Euphorbia prostrata, which are not permitted in food supplements. It also found that the product contained 90 mg of vitamin C, which appeared to exceed the Recommended Dietary Allowance prescribed under the ICMR-NIN Guidelines, 2020.FSSAI also said the product's labelling was misleading, creating the impression of specific regulatory approval, and that it was manufactured and marketed beyond the scope of the firm's FSSAI licence. The prohibition order has been issued under Section 36(3)(b) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor on Monday won the Bankipur assembly bypoll, defeating BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes after securing 64,151 votes, marking a winning start to his electoral career.The bypoll, necessitated after BJP national president Nitin Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha, turned into much more than a contest for a single constituency. Bankipur had remained one of the BJP's safest urban seats for over three decades, with Nabin winning it four consecutive times by comfortable margins.Kishor's victory in the BJP's long-held bastion is likely to be seen as one of the biggest political upsets in Bihar after the assembly elections defeat. The Bankipur victory signals improvement in the party's electoral fortunes and strengthens Kishor's claim of emerging as a credible political alternative in Bihar ahead of the next assembly election.For the BJP, the result is significant because Bankipur has long been among its strongest urban constituencies. Nitin Nabin won the seat in 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2025, each time by comfortable margins.In the 2025 assembly election, Nabin secured 98,299 votes, a 63.25% vote share, defeating the RJD candidate by 51,936 votes. Losing such a seat raises questions about the BJP's ability to retain its traditional urban support base and could prompt a reassessment of its campaign strategy in the next assembly elections.The result carries personal significance for BJP national president Nitin Nabin, who vacated the Bankipur seat after being elected to the Rajya Sabha. The constituency has been synonymous with his political career, with Nabin representing it continuously since 2015 and turning it into one of the BJP's strongest urban bastions in Bihar.Less than a year after Nabin registered a landslide victory in Bankipur, the BJP has lost the seat under his tenure as national president. His absence from the campaign also became a political issue, with NDA leaders, including Union minister Chirag Paswan, accusing him of remaining abroad during the bypoll. The outcome is likely to fuel speculation that sections of the anti-BJP electorate are looking beyond the RJD, with Prashant Kishor emerging as a potential alternative opposition face.The biggest political implication may lie beyond the bypoll itself. Jan Suraaj's victory in Bankipur strengthens the argument that Bihar's politics may no longer remain confined to the NDA versus the RJD-led Mahagathbandhan contest.While one bypoll alone cannot establish a statewide trend, defeating the BJP in one of its strongest constituencies significantly boosts Jan Suraaj's credibility. The result could encourage voters seeking an alternative to the two established alliances and make Prashant Kishor's party a more consequential player in the upcoming Bihar assembly elections.

Article Title: 'Flavouring neutral alcohol isn't right in spirit'
Article Text:
FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has said alcoholic beverage manufacturers cannot add "rum flavour" to rum or "whisky flavour" to whisky and market them as standard products, saying the practice misrepresents the true nature of the beverage and misleads consumers.The regulator said the issue is not the use of permitted flavouring substances, but addition of the flavour of the standardised alcoholic beverage itself, which serves no legitimate purpose. It said the characteristic taste and aroma of products such as rum and whisky should develop naturally through the base ingredients, fermentation, distillation and maturation. However, inspections found that some manufacturers were producing beverages largely from neutral alcohol, which has no characteristic flavour, and then adding identical flavouring substances to recreate the taste and aroma of rum or whisky. Such products, FSSAI said, should be labelled as "rum-flavoured spirit" or "whisky-flavoured spirit", with the front of the pack clearly disclosing their true nature. Laboratory testing of rum and whisky samples from multiple manufacturers found the addition of artificial or nature-identical flavours that masked the products' natural characteristics, rendering them sub-standard under existing regulations, FSSAI said.Based on findings, it prohibited the sale of products manufactured by units of Mohan Rocky Springwater, United Spirits, INBREW Beverages and Associated Alcohol & Breweries. It also inspected Mandexi Distilleries & Breweries in Goa and issued notices to six producers in Maharashtra.FSSAI also objected to the "7 years old blended" claim on an Old Monk XXX Rum variant, saying the product predominantly contained neutral, unmatured spirit, while matured rum spirit accounted for less than 5% of the blend.It said the issue is not representative of the entire industry, noting that many manufacturers continue to produce beverages in compliance with the prescribed standards.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits. It said the practice misrepresents the true nature of the beverage and misleads consumers. The regulator said the issue is not the use of permitted flavouring substances, but addition of the flavour of the standardised alcoholic beverage itself.

Article Title: Military-civil integration key to robust def ecosystem to tackle challenges: Rajnath

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Monday underlined the need to deepen integration between the military and civil components of the defence ministry to foster greater synergy within the defence ecosystem to tackle evolving security and technological challenges, while ensuring institutional memory, stability and the effective application of rules and regulations.Addressing the 85th Armed Forces Headquarters (AFHQ) Civilian Services Day celebrations in Delhi on Aug 3, he emphasised that both uniformed and civil services share the same commitment of ‘Nation First’, and when the objective is singular, every element of the system transforms into national strength.Rajnath underlined that military and administrative integration cannot proceed along separate paths, adding that, as joint and integrated structures develop, there will be a need for continuity and expertise across all areas — policy, administration, human resource management, financial processes, logistics, and institutional knowledge. He highlighted the importance of further enhancing structured cross-exposure between civilian and military officers, suggesting joint training programmes and developmental assignments for both sides to learn from each other’s experiences.“Military officers bring operational experience, a command perspective, and an understanding of warfare, while civilian officers contribute through administrative continuity, policy experience, an understanding of government processes, and institutional memory.When these strengths combine, decision-making becomes more informed, balanced, and effective,” Rajnath said.Explaining with the example of ‘cyber warfare’, the minister stated that if officers of the AFHQ civilian services develop defence-specific common cyber tools leveraging their expertise, it could prove beneficial to the defence forces. He said a forum could be developed for the study of Indian military history, examining it from a civilian perspective, thereby fostering fresh ideas and new perspectives. He expressed confidence that, by leveraging expertise in such areas, AFHQ civilian services will be able to make more meaningful contributions to the defence sector.Rajnath called upon the AFHQ civilian services to evolve into the “strategic brain” of India’s defence management architecture by developing a comprehensive understanding of the defence sector, functioning effectively in a joint environment, and continuously enhancing its expertise to face the emerging challenges.While he acknowledged the AFHQ civilian services for moving ahead in sync with changing times, he asserted that, at a time when modern warfare is driven by technological dynamism, the cadre must move beyond its specific mandate of proper implementation of service rules, regulations & orders.“A military derives its strength not merely from weapons and ammunition, but also from the thousands of unseen hands that always stand in their support. AFHQ Civilian Services is one of these unseen yet decisive forces. It must focus on strengthening the security architecture through research, geo-strategic thinking & innovative ideas. Its active participation in core defence matters is essential as, being a permanent cadre of the Ministry of Defence, it possesses deep domain knowledge,” Rajnath said.
Article Summary: Rajnath Singh underlined the need to deepen integration between the military and civil components of the defence ministry. He emphasised that both uniformed and civil services share the same commitment of ‘Nation First’ He suggested joint training programmes and developmental assignments for both sides to learn from each other’s experiences.

Article Title: Bankipur assembly bypoll: 'Nitish Kumar', 'Lalu Prasad Yadav' lose security deposits
Article Text:
Polling for Bankipur assembly byelection was held on July 30 (Representative photo)

Independent candidates Nitish Kumar and Lalu Prasad Yadav polled 149 and 81 votes respectively
