NEW DELHI: While the spotlight is on Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor , who emerged victorious in his very first electoral outing by wresting BJP bastion Bankipur from the saffron party, "Nitish Kumar" and " Lalu Prasad Yadav " were not as fortunate.The namesakes of Bihar's two political stalwarts and former chief ministers failed to make an impact. The duo, who contested as independents, secured fewer than 150 votes each and lost their deposits.While Lalu Prasad Yadav secured just 81 votes, accounting for a vote share of 0.06%, Nitish Kumar performed slightly better with 149 votes, translating into 0.11% of the total votes polled.They lost their security deposits as per Election Commission rules, which stipulate that candidates who fail to secure at least one-sixth of the total valid votes polled forfeit their deposits, which are then transferred to the treasury.A total of 25 candidates contested the seat, including eight independents.The defeat of the namesakes of Bihar's two political heavyweights came at a time when both leaders are away from active electoral politics. Nitish Kumar resigned as chief minister in March after over two decades in office and was subsequently elected to the Rajya Sabha, while Lalu Prasad Yadav, who has been battling health issues, cannot contest elections and remains barred from holding public office following his conviction in the fodder scam cases.Prashant Kishor defeated Neeraj Kumar, a BJP youth wing leader who was hurriedly fielded by the ruling party after its candidate Abhishek "Bunty" withdrew from the contest at the eleventh hour, citing "family reasons".The former election strategist polled 64,151 votes, defeating Neeraj Kumar by a margin of 19,324 votes. RJD's Rekha Gupta, coincidentally a namesake of BJP leader and Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, finished a distant third with 14,273 votes.The bypoll was necessitated after BJP chief Nitin Nabin resigned following his election to the Rajya Sabha. Nabin had won all four assembly elections from the Bankipur seat since it was created in 2008.The Bankipur assembly constituency, which has nearly 3.8 lakh voters, recorded a turnout of 34.30% in polling held on July 30, significantly lower than the 41.45% turnout recorded in the 2025 Assembly election. The votes were counted on Monday.
Article Summary: The namesakes of Bihar's two political stalwarts failed to make an impact. Nitish Kumar and Lalu Prasad Yadav secured fewer than 150 votes each and lost their deposits. Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor emerged victorious in his first electoral outing.

Some of them operated from special economic zones.An inter-governmental body like the Financial Action Task Force, the Sydney-based APG initiated this study led by Indonesia and UN Office on Drugs and Crime with a team comprised of 24 experts from the govts of Australia, Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Vietnam and UAE.The study examined the emerging nexus between human trafficking and cyber-enabled financial crime, drawing upon the debriefings of 15 Indian nationals repatriated from Myanmar, Lao PDR, and Cambodia between 2023 and 2024.The individuals were recruited under the pretext of high-paying customer-service or IT jobs, transported through Thailand, and then coerced to work in criminal “scam compounds” operated by transnational syndicates, it said.“Victims were mostly young men (20-35 age group) from nine Indian states, recruited via social media or personal networks, who paid upfront fees (Rs 50-70,000). Compounds were run by Chinese-speaking syndicates, with multi-national workforces and strict control (passport confiscation, physical/psychological abuse),” the report has said.The report further revealed that these slave workers were sold between scam compounds, where they were subjected to confinement, violence and debt bondage. “Interception operations and large-scale rescues have revealed victims from a variety of nationalities and regions, suggesting that recruitment practices have expanded beyond solely regional contexts. Workers are forced to conduct investment fraud, impersonation schemes, romance scams, and illegal online gambling platforms, with performance enforced through physical abuse and threats,” it added.Crypto-based financial systems served as core enabling mechanisms.Other examples cited by the agency related to large-scale use of mule accounts and SIM cards from India, which exploited the “vulnerable population”, which were unemployed youth and drug addicts. In one case, muule bank accounts and SIM cards from Punjab were supplied to cyber fraudsters in the Philippines, facilitating scams totalling over Rs 40 crore. The unemployed youth were lured with fake jobs, asked to open accounts and provide their SIMs, which were couriered to the Philippines.

Indian nationals are among victims of several countries trafficked to these cyber hubs and kept as slaves, trained to operate various scams. Cybercrime hubs are controlled by Chinese nationals who also tortured these “slaves” through coercion methods.

Article Title: India gets 101st 'Ramsar' site as Arunachal Pradesh's Glaw Lake joins elite global list of protected wetlands
Article Text:
Glaw Lake in Himachal Pradesh

NEW DELHI: India’s one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the country’s 101st such site and the state’s first to join the elite club for additional care and conservation.Located within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary, Glaw Lake is a pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas and a biodiversity hotspot. The lake is fed by perennial mountain streams and is surrounded by lush vegetation, supporting rich floral diversity.“Every new Ramsar site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,” said Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav while announcing the development on X on Monday.The Glaw Lake wetland has over 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment, underscoring its ecological significance and surrounding landscape.“From 26 Ramsar sites in 2014 to 101 today, this remarkable journey reflects our unwavering commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development,” said Yadav.Globally, there are nearly 2,600 such designated wetlands under the Ramsar Convention.India has the highest number of such wetlands in Asia and third highest in the world after the UK (176) and Mexico (144).Wetlands are land areas covered by water, either temporarily/ seasonally or permanently. These are critical ecosystems that play a significant role in supporting biodiversity, and providing various ecosystem services such as flood control, water supply, food, fibre and raw materials.
Article Summary: India's one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the country's 101st such site and the state’s first to join the elite club for additional care and conservation.

NEW DELHI: Emboldened by the success of the students’ protests here at Jantar Mantar, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM)—the umbrella organisation of farmer groups involved in the anti-farm laws agitation five years ago—on Monday announced that it would restart protests at 100 locations, including Delhi, across India from November 26 - the day which will mark the sixth anniversary of the year-long farmers’ protest, which culminated in the repeal of the three farm laws in December 2021.The protests will demand a law guaranteeing minimum support price (MSP), repeal of all free trade agreements and no India-US FTA, and a comprehensive loan waiver to address rural indebtedness.The SKM’s demand list also includes four other demands such as scrapping of four labour codes; minimum wage of Rs. 31,000 payable to all workers as well as restoration of the previous rural job guarantee scheme; withdrawal of Electricity Privatisation Bill 2025, the Seed Bill 2025, and the NFSA Amendment Bill; and no forceful land acquisition.“The protest will not be called off until all seven principal demands are achieved,” said P Krishnaprasad of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS), a constituent of SKM.“The decisive mass struggle, coordinated with joint platforms and organisations of workers, farmers, agricultural workers, students, youth, women and all other social sections facing the brunt of corporate attack under the NDA regime will advance based on worker-peasant unity to end the prolonged agrarian crisis and labour exploitation, and to build a modern democratic, federal, secular India,” he said while announcing the overall protest plan of the SKM.

Article Title: TRAI revamps 'TRAI MyCall' mobile app to assess voice call quality
Article Text:
TRAI MyCall app gives telecom service providers information on areas where network performance needs improvement

NEW DELHI: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India has revamped the "TRAI MyCall', a mobile application that enables telecom consumers to directly assess and report the voice-calling experience. A citizen-centric digital platform that allows telecom consumers to share real-time feedback on their voice-calling experience, TRAI MyCall app gives telecom service providers (TSPs) information on areas where network performance needs improvement and take targeted corrective measures.TRAI says the revamped app offers instant rating of voice calls through a simple 1-5 star feedback system; reporting of specific issues such as call drops, echo during calls, audio delay, cross connection, voice breaking, one party unable to hear the other, and calls taking too long to connect, which shall be available to respective service provider for corrective action; automatic post-call feedback and coverage test feature to assess signal strength.TRAI chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti said: “Every telecom consumer experiences network quality first-hand. The revamped TRAI MyCall app is expected to strengthen consumer participation feedback on telecom service quality by enabling subscribers to provide immediate and perceived feedback on their call experience. The feedback will assist Telecom Service Providers in identifying network deficiencies and taking corrective measures, enhanced customer satisfaction, and a better overall mobile communication experience.The initiative reinforces TRAI's commitment to a consumer-centric, transparent, and data-driven approach to improving the quality of telecom services. I encourage all mobile users to download the TRAI MyCall application and regularly share their feedback. Every feedback matters, and together we can build a better calling experience for every telecom consumer.”“With over one billion telecom subscribers in India, voice calling remains the most fundamental telecom service and is often the first indicator of network quality experienced by consumers. While network performance is evaluated using technical quality of service (QoS) parameters, the quality of experience (QoE) perceived by consumers also provides an important perspective on service performance. TRAI MyCall bridges this gap by combining consumer feedback with relevant network information to facilitate a more comprehensive assessment of telecom service quality,” TRAI said in a statement.
Article Summary: TRAI says the revamped app offers instant rating of voice calls through a simple 1-5 star feedback system. Report of specific issues such as call drops, echo during calls, audio delay, cross connection, voice breaking, one party unable to hear the other, and calls taking too long to connect.

Article Title: NEET (UG) protests: Gujarat latest BJP-ruled state to order withdrawal of FIRs against demonstrators
Article Text:
Protests were held in various cities of Gujarat seeking the resignation of then education minister Dhrmendra Pradhan (PTI photo)

NEW DELHI: The Gujarat government has directed the state police to withdraw all criminal cases registered against students, youths and others who took part in recent protests over the alleged NEET-UG examination paper leak, officials said on Monday.With this, Gujarat has become the latest BJP-ruled state to withdraw FIRs against NEET protesters. Similar decisions have already been taken by the BJP governments in Assam, Bihar, Delhi and Maharashtra.In a July 31 letter to the state's Director General of Police GS Malik, the Gujarat home department cited the Supreme Court's July 28 judgment restraining police from taking coercive action against minor student protesters and directed the immediate withdrawal of all existing cases.The department instructed the police not to initiate any adverse legal or penal action against individuals who participated in the protests in the state. It further directed that if any FIRs or criminal cases had already been registered against protesters, the legal process for their withdrawal should be completed immediately.The communication, however, did not specify how many FIRs or criminal cases would be withdrawn.Protests were held in Gujarat's Ahmedabad and several other cities in support of demonstrations at Delhi's Jantar Mantar against alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical outfit that had been leading an indefinite sit-in at Jantar Mantar since June 21, called off its protest on July 25 following the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Besides seeking Pradhan's resignation, the CJP had demanded that no action be taken against its members or any NEET protesters across the country.The CJP has repeatedly warned that it would resume its agitation if the FIRs are not withdrawn.Meanwhile, the Supreme Court also clarified on Monday that the expression "criminal antecedents" in its July 28 order on releasing student protesters referred only to those involved in grave and heinous offences, and said states could close or withdraw FIRs against the remaining students in accordance with law.
Article Summary: Gujarat has become the latest BJP-ruled state to withdraw FIRs against NEET protesters. Similar decisions have already been taken by the BJP governments in Assam, Bihar, Delhi and Maharashtra. Supreme Court also clarified on Monday that the expression "criminal antecedents" in its July 28 order on releasing student protesters referred only to those involved in grave and heinous offences.

Article Title: From 2025 washout to historic sweep: How Prashant Kishor put Jan Suraaj on Bihar's electoral map
Article Text:
Jan Suraj party workers celebrated the victory of Prashant Kishor in Bankipur assembly byelection results (Image/PTI)

From assembly setback to bypoll comeback

Why Bankipur mattered

From strategist to politician

Breaking a BJP fortress

Message to BJP leadership

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A political milestone

NEW DELHI: Nearly nine months after Jan Suraaj failed to open its account in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections, party founder Prashant Kishor on Monday secured his first electoral victory. He won the high-profile Bankipur bypoll, giving the fledgling outfit its first-ever seat in the Bihar assembly.Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by 19,324 votes, polling 64,151 votes against Sinha's 44,827, according to the Election Commission.The victory marks Kishor's first electoral success since entering active politics and gives Jan Suraaj its first-ever representation in the Bihar Assembly, offering fresh momentum to a political project that had suffered a crushing setback during its electoral debut last year.The Bankipur result represents a significant political recovery for Kishor, whose Jan Suraaj Party failed to win even a single seat in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections despite contesting more than 200 constituencies.Launched after nearly two years of statewide outreach through the Jan Suraaj padyatra, the party had positioned itself as an alternative to both the NDA and the Mahagathbandhan, focusing on governance reforms, education, employment, migration and corruption rather than traditional caste-based politics.However, the ambitious campaign failed to translate into electoral support.Following the defeat, Kishor publicly accepted full responsibility for the party's performance."We made an honest effort, but it was completely unsuccessful. There's no harm in admitting this. Forget about systemic change; we couldn't even bring about a change in power," he had said after the Assembly election results."There must have been some mistake in our efforts, in our thinking, in the way we explained things. If the public did not show faith in us, then the responsibility for that is completely mine. I take that responsibility 100 per cent on myself."As an act of atonement, Kishor also announced that he would observe a day-long silent fast, saying he had failed to convince the people of Bihar why they should support a new political alternative.At the same time, he ruled out stepping away from politics."I will work twice as hard as you've seen me work over the past three years. There's no question of backing down. There's no turning back until I fulfil my resolve to make Bihar better," he had said.The Bankipur bypoll attracted national attention because of the political stakes involved for both the BJP and Kishor.The election was necessitated after BJP state president Nitin Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha.For nearly three decades, Bankipur had remained one of the BJP's safest urban constituencies. Before Nitin Nabin represented the seat, it had been held by his father, Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha, making it one of the party's strongest bastions in Bihar.In the 2025 assembly elections, Nabin had retained the constituency comfortably by a margin of over 50,000 votes.For Kishor, however, the bypoll was much more than a contest for a single assembly seat.After Jan Suraaj's disappointing electoral debut, the election became a crucial test of whether the party could convert years of grassroots mobilisation into actual electoral success.The contest also marked Kishor's first direct electoral battle after years of shaping campaigns for other political leaders from behind the scenes.Long before entering electoral politics himself, Prashant Kishor had built a reputation as one of India's most influential political strategists.Through his organisation Indian Political Action Committee (I-PAC), he worked on election campaigns for leaders across the political spectrum, including Narendra Modi, Nitish Kumar, Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal, MK Stalin, Jagan Mohan Reddy, Uddhav Thackeray and others.His success as an election strategist later brought him closer to Nitish Kumar, who appointed him as an adviser with cabinet rank after returning as Bihar chief minister in 2015.In 2018, Kishor formally joined the Janata Dal (United) and quickly rose to become the party's national vice-president.However, differences with Nitish Kumar over issues including the Citizenship (Amendment) Act eventually led to his expulsion from the JD(U) in 2020.After briefly attempting to revive the Congress through organisational reforms, Kishor shifted his focus entirely to Bihar.In October 2022, he launched the Jan Suraaj padyatra, travelling across the state to build what he described as a grassroots political movement that would eventually evolve into a full-fledged political party.Although the movement generated considerable public attention, it failed to produce electoral success in the 2025 assembly elections.The Bankipur bypoll now marks Kishor's first major political endorsement as a politician rather than as a strategist.The BJP mounted an extensive campaign to retain Bankipur, deploying senior leaders, ministers and organisational workers to preserve its long-standing hold over the constituency.Despite the party's efforts, Kishor succeeded in wresting away one of the BJP's safest seats.The result is significant not because it alters the numerical balance of power in the Assembly, but because it breaks the perception that Jan Suraaj remains merely a political movement without electoral backing.It also establishes Kishor as an elected legislator for the first time.Beyond the numerical gain of a single seat, the victory gives Jan Suraaj institutional legitimacy.The party will now have a formal voice inside the Bihar assembly and is expected to use the legislative platform to strengthen its organisational presence ahead of future elections.Political observers believe the result could encourage more leaders and workers to join the party while helping it build credibility among voters who were hesitant to back it after the 2025 assembly elections.Although one bypoll does not erase the disappointment of last year's electoral performance, it significantly changes the political narrative around Jan Suraaj—from that of an unsuccessful newcomer to a party capable of winning in one of Bihar's most politically significant constituencies.Even before the counting concluded, Kishor had described the bypoll as something larger than a contest for one assembly seat."It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the Chief Minister of Bihar," he told reporters.Jan Suraaj also celebrated the result on social media, writing on X: "In democracy, the fortress belongs only to the people. Thank you, Bankipur—this is your victory."The Bankipur bypoll does not change Bihar's political arithmetic overnight. The NDA continues to enjoy a comfortable majority in the assembly with 122 seats.However, politically, the result marks an important milestone.After years of being known as the strategist behind other leaders' victories and after suffering a disappointing electoral debut in 2025, Prashant Kishor has finally secured an electoral mandate of his own."I am also congratulating those who lost the election. This is a democracy; there are wins and losses in elections. But the Bankipur election was not an election to elect an MLA. This election was to decide on the BJP-NDA government and its leadership. The people of Bankipur have voted that the central leadership of the BJP should consider it and, in the interest of Bihar, hand over the power of Bihar to a good person," he declared after victory.
Article Summary: Prashant Kishor won the high-profile Bankipur bypoll, giving the fledgling outfit its first-ever seat in the Bihar assembly. He defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by 19,324 votes, polling 64,151 votes against Sinha's 44,827, according to the Election Commission. Jan Suraaj failed to open its account in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections.
